plain: About 12,000 years ago, in a period known as the Younger Dryas, something from space is said to have struck the Earth, causing the great flood of old legends and wiping out an earlier civilization. The podcaster Joe Rogan tells it as a guest, saying you could not stop such an impact and "that's probably what happened during the Younger Dryas impact," and he draws on old texts: the Epic of Gilgamesh, an ancient Mesopotamian poem; the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text, in the translation by R. H. Charles; and the biblical book of Ezekiel. A co-host named Jack, on an episode with a Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, brings up the same idea more loosely as "the reset 12,000 years ago," crediting the researcher Randall Carlson and the writer Graham Hancock. Jack names no impact or flood, only the reset. If true, human history would be much older and more broken than usually told.
